questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical understanding of GitOps-style deployments, environment gating, and basic secrets/config management in Azure DevOps.

## Key Concepts
- Multi-stage YAML pipelines
- Deployment slots and per-environment settings
- Smoke tests for gating deployments
- Secrets via Key Vault and App Configuration integration

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger:
- main
stages:
- stage: Build
  jobs:
  - job: Build
    steps:
    - task: UsePythonVersion@0
      inputs: { versionSpec: '3.x' }
    - script: pip install -r requirements.txt
    - script: pytest --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=. --cov-report=xml
    - task: PublishBuildArtifacts@1
      inputs: { PathtoPublish: '$(Build.ArtifactStagingDirectory)', ArtifactName: 'drop' }
- stage: Deploy-Staging
  dependsOn: Build
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployStaging
    environment: staging
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - task: AzureWebAppContainer@1
            inputs: { appName: '$(webAppName)', imageName: '$(ACR)/fastapi:$(Build.BuildId)', slot: 'staging' }
          - script: |
              curl -sSf https://<host>/health
              curl -sSf https://<host>/ready
            displayName: 'Smoke tests'
- stage: Deploy-Production
  dependsOn: Deploy-Staging
  condition: and(succeeded(), eq(variables['smokeOK'], 'true'))
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployProd
    environment: production
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - task: AzureWebAppContainer@1
            inputs: { appName: '$(webAppName)', imageName: '$(ACR)/fastapi:$(Build.BuildId)', slot: 'production' }
``` 

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you add a rollback path if production deployment fails after swap?
- How would you validate that App Configuration keys map correctly to app settings during runtime?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates multi-region deployment strategies, tenant-aware traffic routing, and production-grade safety controls for an intermediate DevOps engineer role.

## Key Concepts
- Blue/Green deployments across Azure regions
- Azure Front Door per-tenant routing
- Progressive canary rollout by tenant
- Gate enforcement with Azure Policy + OPA
- Drift detection against ARM templates
- Automatic rollback to blue on failure
- Comprehensive logging to Azure Monitor

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger:
  - main

variables:
  blueRegion: 'eastus'
  greenRegion: 'westus2'
  canaryPercentage: 1

stages:
  - stage: PreDeploy_Validation
    jobs:
      - job: PolicyGate
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: AzurePolicyCheck@0
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              resourceGroupName: '$(rgName)'
          - task: Bash@3
            name: 'OPAValidation'
            inputs:
              targetType: 'inline'
              script: |
                opa eval --input tenant-config.json --format json --fail-defined-fail data.policies.deny data.policies.warn

  - stage: DeployBlue
    dependsOn: PreDeploy_Validation
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployToBlueRegion
        environment: 'blue-$(blueRegion)'
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - task: AzureResourceGroupDeployment@3
                  inputs:
                    azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
                    resourceGroupName: '$(rgName)-blue'
                    templateLocation: 'Linked artifact'
                    csmFile: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/templates/api-blue.json'
                - task: AzureCLI@2
                  name: 'RunSmokeTests'
                  inputs:
                    azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
                    scriptType: 'bash'
                    scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
                    inlineScript: |
                      az functionapp test run --name api-blue --test-type smoke
                      
  - stage: DeployGreen
    dependsOn: DeployBlue
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployToGreenRegion
        environment: 'green-$(greenRegion)'
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - task: AzureResourceGroupDeployment@3
                  inputs:
                    azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
                    resourceGroupName: '$(rgName)-green'
                    templateLocation: 'Linked artifact'
                    csmFile: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/templates/api-green.json'
                
  - stage: CanaryRollout
    dependsOn: DeployGreen
    variables:
      tenantList: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/tenants/tenant-list.json'
    jobs:
      - job: PromoteCanary
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: 'RouteCanaryTraffic'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                TENANTS=$(jq -r '.tenants | length * 0.01 | floor' $(tenantList))
                az front door routing-rule update \
                  --frontend-endpoint-name frontend \
                  --name canary-rule \
                  --resource-group $(fdName) \
                  --route-type Performance \
                  --pattern '/*'
                  --backend-pool-name canary-pool
                  
          - task: AzureMonitor@1
            name: 'CheckCanaryMetrics'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              ResourceGroupName: '$(rgName)'
              alertRules:
                - alertName: 'CanaryErrorRate'
                  condition: 'avg(errorRate) > 5'
                  action: 'fail'
          
  - stage: ProductionPromotion
    dependsOn: CanaryRollout
    condition: succeeded('CanaryRollout')
    jobs:
      - job: UpdateFrontDoorRouting
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: 'SwitchTraffic'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az front door routing-rule update \
                  --frontend-endpoint-name frontend \
                  --name production-rule \
                  --resource-group $(fdName) \
                  --backend-pool-name green-pool
                  
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: 'DriftCheck'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az deployment group compare \
                  --resource-group $(rgName)-green \
                  --template-file templates/api-green.json
                  
  - stage: Rollback
    dependsOn: ProductionPromotion
    condition: failed()
    jobs:
      - job: RollbackToBlue
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: 'RevertTraffic'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az front door routing-rule update \
                  --frontend-endpoint-name frontend \
                  --name production-rule \
                  --resource-group $(fdName) \
                  --backend-pool-name blue-pool
                  
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            name: 'NotifyFailure'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az monitor alert create \
                  --name pipeline-failure \
                  --resource-group $(rgName) \
                  --description 'Blue/Green deployment failed - rolled back to blue'
```

**Pipeline Flow Summary**

1. **Pre-Deploy Validation** - Azure Policy gate and OPA policy validation before any deployment
2. **Deploy Blue** - Deploy to blue region with smoke tests
3. **Deploy Green** - Deploy to green region for canary testing
4. **Canary Rollout** - Route 1% of tenants to green, monitor metrics
5. **Production Promotion** - Switch Front Door to green, run drift detection
6. **Automatic Rollback** - On failure, revert Front Door to blue and notify

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assesses end-to-end CI/CD workflows in a PR-driven environment with containerization, basic Kubernetes operations, and observability. Key emphases include reproducible builds, environment isolation, simple health checks, and resource cleanup to prevent leakage.

## Key Concepts
- Azure Pipelines YAML
- npm tasks (install, test, lint)
- Docker image building and pushing
- Azure Container Registry (ACR)
- Azure CLI for AKS cluster management
- kubectl for Kubernetes deployments and services
- Manual and automatic resource cleanup
- Azure Monitor logging integration

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger: none
pr:
  - main
pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: BuildAndTest
        steps:
          - task: NodeTool@0
            inputs:
              versionSpec: '18.x'
          - script: npm ci
            displayName: 'Install dependencies'
          - script: npm test
            displayName: 'Run unit tests'
          - script: npm run lint
            displayName: 'Run ESLint'
          - task: Docker@2
            inputs:
              command: buildAndPush
              repository: '$(ACR_LOGIN_SERVER)/app:$(Build.BuildId)'
              dockerfile: '$(Build.SourcesDirectory)/Dockerfile'
              containerRegistry: '$(ACR_SERVICE_CONNECTION)'

  - stage: Deploy
    dependsOn: Build
    condition: and(succeeded(), eq(variables['Build.Reason'], 'PullRequest'))
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployToAKS
        environment: 'aks-pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)'
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - task: AzureCLI@2
                  inputs:
                    azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)'
                    scriptType: 'bash'
                    scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
                    inlineScript: |
                      PR_ID=$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)
                      NAMESPACE="pr-$PR_ID"
                      kubectl create namespace $NAMESPACE --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
                      kubectl set image deployment/app app=$(ACR_LOGIN_SERVER)/app:$(Build.BuildId) -n $NAMESPACE
                      kubectl expose deployment/app --type=LoadBalancer --port=80 --target-port=3000 -n $NAMESPACE
                      sleep 30
                      SERVICE_IP=$(kubectl get svc app -n $NAMESPACE -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}')
                      curl -f http://$SERVICE_IP/health || exit 1
                - task: AzureMonitor@1
                  inputs:
                    alertResourceGroup: '$(RESOURCE_GROUP)'
                    metricsResourceID: '$(AZURE_MONITOR_RESOURCE_ID)'
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design complex, real-world CI/CD for multi-tenant, region-distributed SaaS applications with GitOps, secret management, and drift handling.

## Key Concepts
- Multi-tenant GitOps repositories with FluxCD per-tenant manifests
- Per-tenant configuration from Azure App Configuration via CSI provider
- Secrets via Azure Key Vault with managed identity (no static credentials)
- Progressive canary rollout across regions using Istio traffic shifting
- Drift detection through FluxCD reconciliation and auto-rollback
- Centralized logging to Azure Monitor Logs (Log Analytics)

## Code Example
```yaml
# Azure DevOps YAML Pipeline - Multi-Tenant AKS GitOps Flow
trigger: none
pr: none

resources:
  repositories:
  - repository: gitops
    type: git
    name: acr-prod/gitops-repo
    ref: main

stages:
- stage: Build
  jobs:
  - job: BuildAndTest
    steps:
    - script: az acr build -r $(acrName) -t $(imageName):$(Build.BuildId) .
      displayName: Build and push to ACR
    - script: npm test -- --coverage
      displayName: Unit & Integration Tests
    - task: Syft@0
      inputs:
        image: $(acrName).azurecr.io/$(imageName):$(Build.BuildId)
        output: cyclonedx-json
        file: sbom.json
    - task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1
      inputs:
        targetPath: sbom.json
        artifact: sbom

- stage: DeployToStaging
  dependsOn: Build
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployStaging
    environment: staging
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - script: |
              cd gitops-repo/clusters/$(location)/staging
              git config user.email "devops@company.com"
              git config user.name "Azure Pipelines"
              cat > values.yaml << EOF
              image:
                tag: "$(Build.BuildId)"
              tenantConfig:
                configStore: "appconfig-$(tenantId)"
              EOF
              git add . && git commit -m "Deploy $(Build.BuildId)" && git push
            displayName: Update GitOps repo

- stage: CanaryPerTenant
  dependsOn: DeployToStaging
  jobs:
  - job: ApplyIstioCanary
    steps:
    - task: Kubernetes@1
      displayName: Apply Istio VirtualService canary
      inputs:
        connectionType: Kubernetes Service Connection
        kubernetesServiceConnection: $(aksCluster)
        namespace: tenant-$(tenantId)
        command: apply
        useConfigurationFile: true
        configuration: canary-manifest.yaml

- stage: RegionalApproval
  dependsOn: CanaryPerTenant
  jobs:
  - job: WaitForApproval
    pool: server
    timeoutInMinutes: 4320
    steps:
    - task: ManualValidation@0
      timeoutInMinutes: 1440
      inputs:
        instructions: 'Approve production deployment to $(location)'
        onTimeout: reject

- stage: ProductionRollout
  dependsOn: RegionalApproval
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployProduction
    environment: production
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - script: kubectl rollout status deployment -n tenant-$(tenantId)
            displayName: Verify rollout
```

## Secret Rotation & Drift Detection

### Secret Rotation
- Use Azure Key Vault with **automatic rotation** policies (time-based or event-based)
- Pods consume secrets via **Azure Key Vault CSI Provider**, which automatically watches for changes
- No pipeline changes needed when secrets rotate—pods remount automatically
- For Azure DevOps service connections, use **workload identity federation** instead of stored secrets

### Drift Detection
- **FluxCD** continuously reconciles git state with cluster state (default every 60 seconds)
- When drift is detected (manual changes, failed rollout, config mismatch), FluxCD marks the resource as `OutOfSync`
- **Alerting**: Configure Azure Monitor Logs to query FluxCD controllers for `level=error` events, triggering Azure Alerts
- **Auto-rollback**: Configure FluxCD with `spec.healthChecks` and `spec.timeout` to auto-heal or rollback on failure
- **Azure Monitor**: Stream FluxCD controller logs to Log Analytics workspace for centralized drift analysis

## Why This Is Asked

- Manual approvals and post‑deploy health checks
- Automatic rollback and Log Analytics auditing

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger:
  branches:
    include:
      - main
pool:
  vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
variables:
  imageName: 'python-microservice'
  registry: 'myacr.azurecr.io'
stages:
- stage: BuildTest
  jobs:
  - job: Build
    steps:
    - checkout: self
    - task: UsePythonVersion@0
      inputs: { versionSpec: '3.x' }
    - script: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install -r requirements.txt
      displayName: 'Install dependencies'
    - script: |
        pytest
      displayName: 'Run tests'
    - script: |
        ruff . --select M,R
      displayName: 'Lint'
    - task: Docker@2
      inputs:
        command: buildAndPush
        containerregistry: '$(registry)'
        repository: '$(imageName)'
        Dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
        tags: '$(Build.BuildId)'
- stage: DeployStaging
  dependsOn: BuildTest
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployStg
    environment: 'staging'
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - script: |
              echo Deploying to staging slot
            displayName: 'Deploy to staging'
          - task: AzureWebAppContainer@1
            inputs:
              appName: 'my-app-staging'
              images: '$(registry)/$(imageName):$(Build.BuildId)'
- stage: ProdGate
  dependsOn: DeployStaging
  jobs:
  - job: ApproveProd
    steps:
    - task: ManualValidation@0
      inputs:
        notifyUsers: '['user@domain.com']'
        timeout: '0:30:00'
        title: 'Approve prod deployment'
        instructions: 'Review health and metrics before production deployment'
- stage: DeployProd
  dependsOn: ProdGate
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployProd
    environment: 'production'
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - script: |
              echo Deploying to production slot
            displayName: 'Deploy to prod'
          - task: AzureWebAppContainer@1
            inputs:
              appName: 'my-app-production'
              images: '$(registry)/$(imageName):$(Build.BuildId)'
          - script: |
              curl -sSf http://my-app-production/health
            displayName: 'Post-deploy health check'
          - powershell: |
              $healthy = (Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://my-app-production/health' -UseBasicParsing).StatusCode -eq 200
              if (-not $healthy) { throw 'Health check failed' }
            displayName: 'Health verification'
- stage: RollbackIfNeeded
  dependsOn: DeployProd
  condition: failed()
  jobs:
  - job: Rollback
    steps:
    - script: |
        echo Rolling back to previous prod image
      displayName: 'Rollback'
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates real-world multi-tenant deployment patterns, including per-tenant isolation, feature flag management, and automated quality gates in enterprise environments.

## Key Concepts

- Azure DevOps YAML pipelines
- AKS with per-tenant namespaces
- App Configuration for feature flags
- k6 synthetic testing
- Azure Monitor logging
- Per-tenant promotion gates with automated rollback

## Code Example

```yaml
name: MultiTenantCanary
trigger: none
stages:
- stage: Deploy
  jobs:
  - deployment: DeployTenant
    strategy:
      matrix:
        tenantA: { tenant: 'tenant-a' }
        tenantB: { tenant: 'tenant-b' }
    environment: 'aks-${tenant}'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    strategy:
      runOnce:
        deploy:
          steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Deploy to AKS namespace'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az aks get-credentials --resource-group $(rgName) --name $(aksCluster)
                kubectl set image deployment/api api=$(containerImage) --namespace=$(tenant)
          - task: AzureAppConfiguration@1
            displayName: 'Fetch feature flags'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              appConfigurationResourceGroup: '$(rgName)'
              appConfigurationName: '$(appConfigName)'
              label: '$(tenant)'
          - task: Bash@3
            displayName: 'Run k6 synthetic tests'
            env:
              TENANT_URL: 'https://$(tenant).api.example.com'
            inputs:
              filePath: 'tests/k6-synthetic.sh'
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Check health and gate promotion'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                HEALTH=$(curl -s https://$(tenant).api.example.com/health)
                if [ "$HEALTH" != "healthy" ]; then
                  echo "##vso[task.logissue type=error]Health check failed for $(tenant)"
                  exit 1
                fi
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Rollback on failure'
            condition: failed()
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: '$(azureServiceConnection)'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                kubectl rollout undo deployment/api --namespace=$(tenant)
                echo "Rolled back $(tenant) to previous revision"
          - task: AzureMonitor@1
            displayName: 'Log to Azure Monitor'
            inputs:
              azureResourceGroup: '$(rgName)'
              resourceType: 'Container Insights'
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical ability to wire Boards, Repos, Pipelines, and Environments into a single PR governance flow.

## Key Concepts

- Branch Policies: Linked Work Items
- PR Validation: Title pattern check
- Build Validation: PR validations
- Environments: Staging auto-deploy, Prod gate

## Code Example

```yaml
trigger:
  - main
pr:
  branches:
    include:
      - main
jobs:
- job: PRValidation
  pool:
    vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
  steps:
  - bash: |
      if [[ -z "$(System.PullRequest.Title)" || "$(System.PullRequest.Title)" != *"ABC-"* ]]; then
        echo "PR title must include work item like ABC-123"; exit 1
      fi
  - script: npm ci && npm test
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adapt to multi-repo scenarios?
- How would you monitor and audit policy violations?
